controller_configuration.locks_yaml:
# Locks to stop the twist mux.
# For each lock:
# - topic   : input topic that provides the lock; it must be of type std_msgs::Bool?!!! 
# - timeout : == 0.0 -> not used
#              > 0.0 -> the lock is supposed to published at a certain frequency in order
#                       to detect that the publisher is alive; the timeout in seconds allows
#                       to detect that, and if the publisher dies we will enable the lock
# - priority: priority in the range [0, 255], so all the topics with priority lower than it
#             will be stopped/disabled

/twist_mux:
  ros__parameters:
    locks:
      joystick:
        topic   : joy_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 100
      assisted_teleop:
        topic   : assisted_teleop_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 200
      charging:
        topic   : power/is_charging
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 210

# Input topics handled/muxed by the twist mux.
# For each topic:
# - name    : name identifier to select the topic
# - topic   : input topic of geometry_msgs::Twist type
# - timeout : timeout in seconds to start discarding old messages, and use 0.0 speed instead
# - priority: priority in the range [0, 255]; the higher the more priority over other topics

/twist_mux:
  ros__parameters:
    topics:
      navigation:
        topic   : cmd_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 10
      keyboard:
        topic   : key_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 90

source_context.controller_source_scope: Static public configuration licenses source-qualified priority rules. Any supplied runtime snapshots are observed parameter-service and ROS-graph evidence only at their explicit native simulated-clock stamps. Absent or masked snapshots remain unknown. Two matching boundary snapshots do not prove continuous wiring or absence of intervening changes. Neither configuration nor graph alone proves message delivery, applied torque, physical arrival, or a unique physical cause.
source_context.event_scope: Planner/progress failure and clearing-request logs are software execution evidence, not direct geometry or unique physical causes. No supplied costmap/scan/path measurement proves an obstacle or moving obstacle. A clearing request does not prove completed clearing.
source_context.indicator_semantics: The released component maps /joy_priority to manual selection and /power/is_charging to charging selection. In this adapted simulation these Bool states are supervisor interlock indicators, not proof of a human joystick action or physical battery charging. The genuine public controller configuration is supplied below. Only measurements explicitly visible in the packet can establish applied output or physical motion; missing measurements remain unknown.
source_context.localization_semantics: The original callback appends a high-uncertainty diagnostic after its count exceeds five samples with mean XY covariance or orientation variance above .2. Its count decrements on low samples; this is preserved, not a new localization detector.
source_context.missingness: Unavailable evidence is unknown; do not replace it with false, zero, success or normal behavior.
source_context.motion_window_scope: Odometry is restricted to recorded simulated ROS stamps within instrumented driver observations of acceptance-to-result/disposition. The recorded sample extent, boundary gaps and maximum internal gap remain explicit. Driver observations are software protocol evidence, not physical arrival. Command summaries retain their recording scope; no receipt-clock conversion or TF transform is inferred.
source_context.navigation_task_scope: This adapted no-arm simulation executes navigation only. Recorded task labels are reported software metadata, not evidence of manipulation, item delivery or an independently verified room/zone. A label such as kitchen is not a measured semantic location. Do not invent unexecuted skills.
source_context.outcome_measurement_scope: Navigation/task status is a reported software outcome. Reported success alone does not establish measured motion or physical goal attainment. A software status and instrumented motion observation may differ; describe both when visible without inventing a reason for the difference. Unavailable motion or goal/pose/frame/time evidence remains unknown.
source_context.timing_scope: Requested window follows upstream task bookkeeping and its sec.nanosec conversion. A recorded navigation success does not establish a safety-speed policy or a measured cause of slowness.

controller_configuration.locks_yaml:
# Locks to stop the twist mux.
# For each lock:
# - topic   : input topic that provides the lock; it must be of type std_msgs::Bool?!!! 
# - timeout : == 0.0 -> not used
#              > 0.0 -> the lock is supposed to published at a certain frequency in order
#                       to detect that the publisher is alive; the timeout in seconds allows
#                       to detect that, and if the publisher dies we will enable the lock
# - priority: priority in the range [0, 255], so all the topics with priority lower than it
#             will be stopped/disabled

/twist_mux:
  ros__parameters:
    locks:
      joystick:
        topic   : joy_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 100
      assisted_teleop:
        topic   : assisted_teleop_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 200
      charging:
        topic   : power/is_charging
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 210
controller_configuration.topics_yaml:
# Input topics handled/muxed by the twist mux.
# For each topic:
# - name    : name identifier to select the topic
# - topic   : input topic of geometry_msgs::Twist type
# - timeout : timeout in seconds to start discarding old messages, and use 0.0 speed instead
# - priority: priority in the range [0, 255]; the higher the more priority over other topics

/twist_mux:
  ros__parameters:
    topics:
      navigation:
        topic   : cmd_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 10
      keyboard:
        topic   : key_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 90
      rviz:
        topic   : rviz_joy_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 100
      joystick:
        topic   : joy_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 100
      webgui_joystick:
        topic   : tab_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 100
      assisted_teleop:
        topic   : assisted_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 200
      docking:
        topic   : docking_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 210

source_context.timing_scope: Requested window follows upstream task bookkeeping and its sec.nanosec conversion. A recorded navigation success does not establish a safety-speed policy or a measured cause of slowness.

controller_configuration.locks_yaml:
# Locks to stop the twist mux.
# For each lock:
# - topic   : input topic that provides the lock; it must be of type std_msgs::Bool?!!! 
# - timeout : == 0.0 -> not used
#              > 0.0 -> the lock is supposed to published at a certain frequency in order
#                       to detect that the publisher is alive; the timeout in seconds allows
#                       to detect that, and if the publisher dies we will enable the lock
# - priority: priority in the range [0, 255], so all the topics with priority lower than it
#             will be stopped/disabled

/twist_mux:
  ros__parameters:
    locks:
      joystick:
        topic   : joy_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 100
      assisted_teleop:
        topic   : assisted_teleop_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 200
      charging:
        topic   : power/is_charging
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 210
controller_configuration.topics_yaml:
# Input topics handled/muxed by the twist mux.
# For each topic:
# - name    : name identifier to select the topic
# - topic   : input topic of geometry_msgs::Twist type
# - timeout : timeout in seconds to start discarding old messages, and use 0.0 speed instead
# - priority: priority in the range [0, 255]; the higher the more priority over other topics

/twist_mux:
  ros__parameters:
    topics:
      navigation:
        topic   : cmd_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 10

        topic   : key_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 90

        topic   : rviz_joy_vel

        priority: 100

        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 100

        topic   : tab_vel

        priority: 100
      assisted_teleop:

        priority: 200

controller_configuration.locks_yaml:
# Locks to stop the twist mux.
# For each lock:
# - topic   : input topic that provides the lock; it must be of type std_msgs::Bool?!!! 
# - timeout : == 0.0 -> not used
#              > 0.0 -> the lock is supposed to published at a certain frequency in order
#                       to detect that the publisher is alive; the timeout in seconds allows
#                       to detect that, and if the publisher dies we will enable the lock
# - priority: priority in the range [0, 255], so all the topics with priority lower than it
#             will be stopped/disabled

/twist_mux:
  ros__parameters:
    locks:
      joystick:
        topic   : joy_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 100
      assisted_teleop:
        topic   : assisted_teleop_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 200
      charging:
        topic   : power/is_charging
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 210

Any supplied runtime snapshots are observed parameter-service and ROS-graph evidence only at their explicit native simulated-clock stamps. Absent or masked snapshots remain unknown. source_context.event_scope: Planner/progress failure and clearing-request logs are software execution evidence, not direct geometry or unique physical causes. No supplied costmap/scan/path measurement proves an obstacle or moving obstacle. A clearing request does not prove completed clearing.
source_context.indicator_semantics: The released component maps /joy_priority to manual selection and /power/is_charging to charging selection. In this adapted simulation these Bool states are supervisor interlock indicators, not proof of a human joystick action or physical battery charging. The genuine public controller configuration is supplied below. Only measurements explicitly visible in the packet can establish applied output or physical motion; missing measurements remain unknown.
source_context.localization_semantics: The original callback appends a high-uncertainty diagnostic after its count exceeds five samples with mean XY covariance or orientation variance above .2. Its count decrements on low samples; this is preserved, not a new localization detector.
source_context.missingness: Unavailable evidence is unknown; do not replace it with false, zero, success or normal behavior.
source_context.motion_window_scope: Odometry is restricted to recorded simulated ROS stamps within instrumented driver observations of acceptance-to-result/disposition. The recorded sample extent, boundary gaps and maximum internal gap remain explicit. Driver observations are software protocol evidence, not physical arrival. Command summaries retain their recording scope; no receipt-clock conversion or TF transform is inferred.
source_context.navigation_task_scope: This adapted no-arm simulation executes navigation only. Recorded task labels are reported software metadata, not evidence of manipulation, item delivery or an independently verified room/zone. A label such as kitchen is not a measured semantic location. Do not invent unexecuted skills.
source_context.outcome_measurement_scope: Navigation/task status is a reported software outcome. Reported success alone does not establish measured motion or physical goal attainment. A software status and instrumented motion observation may differ; describe both when visible without inventing a reason for the difference. Unavailable motion or goal/pose/frame/time evidence remains unknown.
source_context.timing_scope: Requested window follows upstream task bookkeeping and its sec.nanosec conversion. A recorded navigation success does not establish a safety-speed policy or a measured cause of slowness.

controller_configuration.locks_yaml:
# Locks to stop the twist mux.
# For each lock:
# - topic   : input topic that provides the lock; it must be of type std_msgs::Bool?!!! 
# - timeout : == 0.0 -> not used
#              > 0.0 -> the lock is supposed to published at a certain frequency in order
#                       to detect that the publisher is alive; the timeout in seconds allows
#                       to detect that, and if the publisher dies we will enable the lock
# - priority: priority in the range [0, 255], so all the topics with priority lower than it
#             will be stopped/disabled

/twist_mux:
  ros__parameters:
    locks:
      joystick:
        topic   : joy_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 100
      assisted_teleop:
        topic   : assisted_teleop_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 200
      charging:
        topic   : power/is_charging
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 210
controller_configuration.topics_yaml:
# Input topics handled/muxed by the twist mux.
# For each topic:
# - name    : name identifier to select the topic
# - topic   : input topic of geometry_msgs::Twist type
# - timeout : timeout in seconds to start discarding old messages, and use 0.0 speed instead
# - priority: priority in the range [0, 255]; the higher the more priority over other topics

/twist_mux:
  ros__parameters:
    topics:
      navigation:
        topic   : cmd_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 10
      keyboard:
        topic   : key_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 90
      rviz:
        topic   : rviz_joy_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 100
      joystick:
        topic   : joy_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 100
      webgui_joystick:
        topic   : tab_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 100
      assisted_teleop:
        topic   : assisted_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 200
      docking:
        topic   : docking_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 210

controller_configuration.locks_yaml:
# Locks to stop the twist mux.
# For each lock:
# - topic   : input topic that provides the lock; it must be of type std_msgs::Bool?!!! 
# - timeout : == 0.0 -> not used
#              > 0.0 -> the lock is supposed to published at a certain frequency in order
#                       to detect that the publisher is alive; the timeout in seconds allows
#                       to detect that, and if the publisher dies we will enable the lock
# - priority: priority in the range [0, 255], so all the topics with priority lower than it
#             will be stopped/disabled

/twist_mux:
  ros__parameters:
    locks:
      joystick:
        topic   : joy_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 100
      assisted_teleop:
        topic   : assisted_teleop_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 200
      charging:
        topic   : power/is_charging
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 210
controller_configuration.topics_yaml:
# Input topics handled/muxed by the twist mux.
# For each topic:
# - name    : name identifier to select the topic
# - topic   : input topic of geometry_msgs::Twist type
# - timeout : timeout in seconds to start discarding old messages, and use 0.0 speed instead
# - priority: priority in the range [0, 255]; the higher the more priority over other topics

/twist_mux:
  ros__parameters:
    topics:
      navigation:
        topic   : cmd_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 10
      keyboard:
        topic   : key_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 90
      rviz:
        topic   : rviz_joy_vel

        priority: 100

        topic   : joy_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 100
      webgui_joystick:
        topic   : tab_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 100
      assisted_teleop:
        topic   : assisted_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 200
      docking:

controller_configuration.locks_yaml:
# Locks to stop the twist mux.
# For each lock:
# - topic   : input topic that provides the lock; it must be of type std_msgs::Bool?!!! 
# - timeout : == 0.0 -> not used
#              > 0.0 -> the lock is supposed to published at a certain frequency in order
#                       to detect that the publisher is alive; the timeout in seconds allows
#                       to detect that, and if the publisher dies we will enable the lock
# - priority: priority in the range [0, 255], so all the topics with priority lower than it
#             will be stopped/disabled

/twist_mux:
  ros__parameters:
    locks:
      joystick:
        topic   : joy_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 100
      assisted_teleop:
        topic   : assisted_teleop_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 200
      charging:
        topic   : power/is_charging
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 210
controller_configuration.topics_yaml:
# Input topics handled/muxed by the twist mux.
# For each topic:
# - name    : name identifier to select the topic
# - topic   : input topic of geometry_msgs::Twist type
# - timeout : timeout in seconds to start discarding old messages, and use 0.0 speed instead
# - priority: priority in the range [0, 255]; the higher the more priority over other topics

/twist_mux:
  ros__parameters:
    topics:
      navigation:
        topic   : cmd_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 10
      keyboard:
        topic   : key_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 90
      rviz:
        topic   : rviz_joy_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 100
      joystick:
        topic   : joy_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 100
      webgui_joystick:
        topic   : tab_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 100
      assisted_teleop:
        topic   : assisted_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 200
      docking:
        topic   : docking_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 210

source_context.controller_source_scope: Static public configuration licenses source-qualified priority rules. Any supplied runtime snapshots are observed parameter-service and ROS-graph evidence only at their explicit native simulated-clock stamps. Absent or masked snapshots remain unknown. Two matching boundary snapshots do not prove continuous wiring or absence of intervening changes. Neither configuration nor graph alone proves message delivery, applied torque, physical arrival, or a unique physical cause.
source_context.event_scope: Planner/progress failure and clearing-request logs are software execution evidence, not direct geometry or unique physical causes. No supplied costmap/scan/path measurement proves an obstacle or moving obstacle. A clearing request does not prove completed clearing.
source_context.indicator_semantics: The released component maps /joy_priority to manual selection and /power/is_charging to charging selection. In this adapted simulation these Bool states are supervisor interlock indicators, not proof of a human joystick action or physical battery charging. The genuine public controller configuration is supplied below. Only measurements explicitly visible in the packet can establish applied output or physical motion; missing measurements remain unknown.
source_context.localization_semantics: The original callback appends a high-uncertainty diagnostic after its count exceeds five samples with mean XY covariance or orientation variance above .2. Its count decrements on low samples; this is preserved, not a new localization detector.
source_context.missingness: Unavailable evidence is unknown; do not replace it with false, zero, success or normal behavior.
source_context.motion_window_scope: Odometry is restricted to recorded simulated ROS stamps within instrumented driver observations of acceptance-to-result/disposition. The recorded sample extent, boundary gaps and maximum internal gap remain explicit. Driver observations are software protocol evidence, not physical arrival. Command summaries retain their recording scope; no receipt-clock conversion or TF transform is inferred.
source_context.navigation_task_scope: This adapted no-arm simulation executes navigation only. Recorded task labels are reported software metadata, not evidence of manipulation, item delivery or an independently verified room/zone. A label such as kitchen is not a measured semantic location. Do not invent unexecuted skills.
source_context.outcome_measurement_scope: Navigation/task status is a reported software outcome. Reported success alone does not establish measured motion or physical goal attainment. A software status and instrumented motion observation may differ; describe both when visible without inventing a reason for the difference. Unavailable motion or goal/pose/frame/time evidence remains unknown.
source_context.timing_scope: Requested window follows upstream task bookkeeping and its sec.nanosec conversion. A recorded navigation success does not establish a safety-speed policy or a measured cause of slowness.

visible_evidence.command_observation: Navigation input command samples included nonzero vectors. Recorded controller-output command vectors were zero; commands do not prove applied torque.
visible_evidence.controller_configuration: Public static configuration: navigation input priority 10; manual-priority lock 100; charging lock 210. Active locks inhibit lower-priority inputs; equal/higher-priority inputs may remain eligible.
visible_evidence.interlock_indicator: The supervisor manual-priority interlock indicator was true; it does not itself prove human operation.
visible_evidence.observed_action_window: The recorded action UUID was accepted, then returned software success; these driver observations are not physical arrival.
visible_evidence.odometry: Sampled controller odometry estimated 8.18 m of XY path distance in the odom frame within the observed action window; no transform to map is supplied.
visible_evidence.requested_goal: A navigation request targeted map-frame pose (-4.56, 0.93).

controller_configuration.locks_yaml:
# Locks to stop the twist mux.
# For each lock:
# - topic   : input topic that provides the lock; it must be of type std_msgs::Bool?!!! 
# - timeout : == 0.0 -> not used
#              > 0.0 -> the lock is supposed to published at a certain frequency in order
#                       to detect that the publisher is alive; the timeout in seconds allows
#                       to detect that, and if the publisher dies we will enable the lock
# - priority: priority in the range [0, 255], so all the topics with priority lower than it
#             will be stopped/disabled

/twist_mux:
  ros__parameters:
    locks:
      joystick:
        topic   : joy_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 100
      assisted_teleop:
        topic   : assisted_teleop_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 200
      charging:
        topic   : power/is_charging
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 210
controller_configuration.topics_yaml:
# Input topics handled/muxed by the twist mux.
# For each topic:
# - name    : name identifier to select the topic
# - topic   : input topic of geometry_msgs::Twist type
# - timeout : timeout in seconds to start discarding old messages, and use 0.0 speed instead
# - priority: priority in the range [0, 255]; the higher the more priority over other topics

/twist_mux:
  ros__parameters:
    topics:
      navigation:
        topic   : cmd_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 10
      keyboard:
        topic   : key_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 90
      rviz:
        topic   : rviz_joy_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 100
      joystick:
        topic   : joy_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 100
      webgui_joystick:
        topic   : tab_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 100
      assisted_teleop:
        topic   : assisted_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 200
      docking:
        topic   : docking_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 210

Any supplied runtime snapshots are observed parameter-service and ROS-graph evidence only at their explicit native simulated-clock stamps. Absent or masked snapshots remain unknown. Two matching boundary snapshots do not prove continuous wiring or absence of intervening changes. source_context.event_scope: Planner/progress failure and clearing-request logs are software execution evidence, not direct geometry or unique physical causes. No supplied costmap/scan/path measurement proves an obstacle or moving obstacle. A clearing request does not prove completed clearing.
source_context.indicator_semantics: The released component maps /joy_priority to manual selection and /power/is_charging to charging selection. In this adapted simulation these Bool states are supervisor interlock indicators, not proof of a human joystick action or physical battery charging. The genuine public controller configuration is supplied below. Only measurements explicitly visible in the packet can establish applied output or physical motion; missing measurements remain unknown.
source_context.localization_semantics: The original callback appends a high-uncertainty diagnostic after its count exceeds five samples with mean XY covariance or orientation variance above .2. Its count decrements on low samples; this is preserved, not a new localization detector.
source_context.missingness: Unavailable evidence is unknown; do not replace it with false, zero, success or normal behavior.
source_context.motion_window_scope: Odometry is restricted to recorded simulated ROS stamps within instrumented driver observations of acceptance-to-result/disposition. The recorded sample extent, boundary gaps and maximum internal gap remain explicit. Driver observations are software protocol evidence, not physical arrival. Command summaries retain their recording scope; no receipt-clock conversion or TF transform is inferred.
source_context.navigation_task_scope: This adapted no-arm simulation executes navigation only. Recorded task labels are reported software metadata, not evidence of manipulation, item delivery or an independently verified room/zone. A label such as kitchen is not a measured semantic location. Do not invent unexecuted skills.
source_context.outcome_measurement_scope: Navigation/task status is a reported software outcome. Reported success alone does not establish measured motion or physical goal attainment. Unavailable motion or goal/pose/frame/time evidence remains unknown.
source_context.timing_scope: Requested window follows upstream task bookkeeping and its sec.nanosec conversion. A recorded navigation success does not establish a safety-speed policy or a measured cause of slowness.

controller_configuration.locks_yaml:
# Locks to stop the twist mux.
# For each lock:
# - topic   : input topic that provides the lock; it must be of type std_msgs::Bool?!!! 
# - timeout : == 0.0 -> not used
#              > 0.0 -> the lock is supposed to published at a certain frequency in order
#                       to detect that the publisher is alive; the timeout in seconds allows
#                       to detect that, and if the publisher dies we will enable the lock
# - priority: priority in the range [0, 255], so all the topics with priority lower than it
#             will be stopped/disabled

/twist_mux:
  ros__parameters:
    locks:
      joystick:
        topic   : joy_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 100
      assisted_teleop:
        topic   : assisted_teleop_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 200
      charging:
        topic   : power/is_charging
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 210
controller_configuration.topics_yaml:
# Input topics handled/muxed by the twist mux.
# For each topic:
# - name    : name identifier to select the topic
# - topic   : input topic of geometry_msgs::Twist type
# - timeout : timeout in seconds to start discarding old messages, and use 0.0 speed instead
# - priority: priority in the range [0, 255]; the higher the more priority over other topics

/twist_mux:
  ros__parameters:
    topics:
      navigation:
        topic   : cmd_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 10
      keyboard:
        topic   : key_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 90
      rviz:
        topic   : rviz_joy_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 100
      joystick:
        topic   : joy_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 100
      webgui_joystick:
        topic   : tab_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 100
      assisted_teleop:
        topic   : assisted_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 200
      docking:
        topic   : docking_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 210

source_context.controller_source_scope: Static public configuration licenses source-qualified priority rules. Any supplied runtime snapshots are observed parameter-service and ROS-graph evidence only at their explicit native simulated-clock stamps. Absent or masked snapshots remain unknown. Two matching boundary snapshots do not prove continuous wiring or absence of intervening changes. Neither configuration nor graph alone proves message delivery, applied torque, physical arrival, or a unique physical cause.
source_context.event_scope: Planner/progress failure and clearing-request logs are software execution evidence, not direct geometry or unique physical causes. No supplied costmap/scan/path measurement proves an obstacle or moving obstacle. A clearing request does not prove completed clearing.
source_context.indicator_semantics: The released component maps /joy_priority to manual selection and /power/is_charging to charging selection. In this adapted simulation these Bool states are supervisor interlock indicators, not proof of a human joystick action or physical battery charging. The genuine public controller configuration is supplied below. Only measurements explicitly visible in the packet can establish applied output or physical motion; missing measurements remain unknown.
source_context.localization_semantics: The original callback appends a high-uncertainty diagnostic after its count exceeds five samples with mean XY covariance or orientation variance above .2. Its count decrements on low samples; this is preserved, not a new localization detector.
source_context.missingness: Unavailable evidence is unknown; do not replace it with false, zero, success or normal behavior.
source_context.motion_window_scope: Odometry is restricted to recorded simulated ROS stamps within instrumented driver observations of acceptance-to-result/disposition. The recorded sample extent, boundary gaps and maximum internal gap remain explicit. Driver observations are software protocol evidence, not physical arrival. Command summaries retain their recording scope; no receipt-clock conversion or TF transform is inferred.
source_context.navigation_task_scope: This adapted no-arm simulation executes navigation only. Recorded task labels are reported software metadata, not evidence of manipulation, item delivery or an independently verified room/zone. A label such as kitchen is not a measured semantic location. Do not invent unexecuted skills.
source_context.outcome_measurement_scope: Navigation/task status is a reported software outcome. Reported success alone does not establish measured motion or physical goal attainment. A software status and instrumented motion observation may differ; describe both when visible without inventing a reason for the difference. Unavailable motion or goal/pose/frame/time evidence remains unknown.
source_context.timing_scope: Requested window follows upstream task bookkeeping and its sec.nanosec conversion. A recorded navigation success does not establish a safety-speed policy or a measured cause of slowness.

controller_configuration.locks_yaml:
# Locks to stop the twist mux.
# For each lock:
# - topic   : input topic that provides the lock; it must be of type std_msgs::Bool?!!! 
# - timeout : == 0.0 -> not used
#              > 0.0 -> the lock is supposed to published at a certain frequency in order
#                       to detect that the publisher is alive; the timeout in seconds allows
#                       to detect that, and if the publisher dies we will enable the lock
# - priority: priority in the range [0, 255], so all the topics with priority lower than it
#             will be stopped/disabled

/twist_mux:
  ros__parameters:
    locks:
      joystick:
        topic   : joy_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 100
      assisted_teleop:
        topic   : assisted_teleop_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 200
      charging:
        topic   : power/is_charging
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 210
controller_configuration.topics_yaml:
# Input topics handled/muxed by the twist mux.
# For each topic:
# - name    : name identifier to select the topic
# - topic   : input topic of geometry_msgs::Twist type
# - timeout : timeout in seconds to start discarding old messages, and use 0.0 speed instead
# - priority: priority in the range [0, 255]; the higher the more priority over other topics

/twist_mux:
  ros__parameters:
    topics:
      navigation:
        topic   : cmd_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 10
      keyboard:
        topic   : key_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 90
      rviz:
        topic   : rviz_joy_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 100
      joystick:
        topic   : joy_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 100
      webgui_joystick:
        topic   : tab_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 100
      assisted_teleop:
        topic   : assisted_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 200
      docking:
        topic   : docking_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 210

source_context.indicator_semantics: The released component maps /joy_priority to manual selection and /power/is_charging to charging selection. In this adapted simulation these Bool states are supervisor interlock indicators, not proof of a human joystick action or physical battery charging. The genuine public controller configuration is supplied below. Only measurements explicitly visible in the packet can establish applied output or physical motion; missing measurements remain unknown.
source_context.localization_semantics: The original callback appends a high-uncertainty diagnostic after its count exceeds five samples with mean XY covariance or orientation variance above .2. Its count decrements on low samples; this is preserved, not a new localization detector.

source_context.motion_window_scope: Odometry is restricted to recorded simulated ROS stamps within instrumented driver observations of acceptance-to-result/disposition. The recorded sample extent, boundary gaps and maximum internal gap remain explicit. Driver observations are software protocol evidence, not physical arrival. Command summaries retain their recording scope; no receipt-clock conversion or TF transform is inferred.
source_context.navigation_task_scope: This adapted no-arm simulation executes navigation only. Recorded task labels are reported software metadata, not evidence of manipulation, item delivery or an independently verified room/zone. A label such as kitchen is not a measured semantic location. Do not invent unexecuted skills.
source_context.outcome_measurement_scope: Navigation/task status is a reported software outcome. Reported success alone does not establish measured motion or physical goal attainment. A software status and instrumented motion observation may differ; describe both when visible without inventing a reason for the difference. Unavailable motion or goal/pose/frame/time evidence remains unknown.
source_context.timing_scope: Requested window follows upstream task bookkeeping and its sec.nanosec conversion. A recorded navigation success does not establish a safety-speed policy or a measured cause of slowness.

controller_configuration.locks_yaml:
# Locks to stop the twist mux.
# For each lock:
# - topic   : input topic that provides the lock; it must be of type std_msgs::Bool?!!! 
# - timeout : == 0.0 -> not used
#              > 0.0 -> the lock is supposed to published at a certain frequency in order
#                       to detect that the publisher is alive; the timeout in seconds allows
#                       to detect that, and if the publisher dies we will enable the lock
# - priority: priority in the range [0, 255], so all the topics with priority lower than it
#             will be stopped/disabled

/twist_mux:
  ros__parameters:
    locks:
      joystick:
        topic   : joy_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 100
      assisted_teleop:
        topic   : assisted_teleop_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 200
      charging:
        topic   : power/is_charging
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 210
controller_configuration.topics_yaml:
# Input topics handled/muxed by the twist mux.

# - name    : name identifier to select the topic

# - priority: priority in the range [0, 255]; the higher the more priority over other topics

/twist_mux:
  ros__parameters:
    topics:
      navigation:
        topic   : cmd_vel

        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 100

        priority: 100
      assisted_teleop:
        topic   : assisted_vel
        timeout : 0.5

# Locks to stop the twist mux.
# For each lock:
# - topic   : input topic that provides the lock; it must be of type std_msgs::Bool?!!! 
# - timeout : == 0.0 -> not used
#              > 0.0 -> the lock is supposed to published at a certain frequency in order
#                       to detect that the publisher is alive; the timeout in seconds allows
#                       to detect that, and if the publisher dies we will enable the lock
# - priority: priority in the range [0, 255], so all the topics with priority lower than it
#             will be stopped/disabled

/twist_mux:
  ros__parameters:
    locks:
      joystick:
        topic   : joy_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 100
      assisted_teleop:
        topic   : assisted_teleop_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 200

        priority: 210

controller_configuration.locks_yaml:
# Locks to stop the twist mux.
# For each lock:
# - topic   : input topic that provides the lock; it must be of type std_msgs::Bool?!!! 
# - timeout : == 0.0 -> not used
#              > 0.0 -> the lock is supposed to published at a certain frequency in order
#                       to detect that the publisher is alive; the timeout in seconds allows
#                       to detect that, and if the publisher dies we will enable the lock
# - priority: priority in the range [0, 255], so all the topics with priority lower than it
#             will be stopped/disabled

/twist_mux:
  ros__parameters:
    locks:
      joystick:
        topic   : joy_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 100
      assisted_teleop:
        topic   : assisted_teleop_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 200
      charging:
        topic   : power/is_charging
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 210

source_context.timing_scope: Requested window follows upstream task bookkeeping and its sec.nanosec conversion. A recorded navigation success does not establish a safety-speed policy or a measured cause of slowness.

# Locks to stop the twist mux.
# For each lock:

controller_configuration.locks_yaml:
# Locks to stop the twist mux.
# For each lock:
# - topic   : input topic that provides the lock; it must be of type std_msgs::Bool?!!! 
# - timeout : == 0.0 -> not used
#              > 0.0 -> the lock is supposed to published at a certain frequency in order
#                       to detect that the publisher is alive; the timeout in seconds allows
#                       to detect that, and if the publisher dies we will enable the lock
# - priority: priority in the range [0, 255], so all the topics with priority lower than it
#             will be stopped/disabled

/twist_mux:
  ros__parameters:
    locks:
      joystick:
        topic   : joy_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 100
      assisted_teleop:
        topic   : assisted_teleop_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 200
      charging:
        topic   : power/is_charging
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 210

controller_configuration.locks_yaml:
# Locks to stop the twist mux.
# For each lock:
# - topic   : input topic that provides the lock; it must be of type std_msgs::Bool?!!! 
# - timeout : == 0.0 -> not used
#              > 0.0 -> the lock is supposed to published at a certain frequency in order
#                       to detect that the publisher is alive; the timeout in seconds allows
#                       to detect that, and if the publisher dies we will enable the lock
# - priority: priority in the range [0, 255], so all the topics with priority lower than it
#             will be stopped/disabled

/twist_mux:
  ros__parameters:
    locks:
      joystick:
        topic   : joy_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 100
      assisted_teleop:
        topic   : assisted_teleop_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 200
      charging:
        topic   : power/is_charging
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 210

# Input topics handled/muxed by the twist mux.
# For each topic:
# - name    : name identifier to select the topic
# - topic   : input topic of geometry_msgs::Twist type
# - timeout : timeout in seconds to start discarding old messages, and use 0.0 speed instead
# - priority: priority in the range [0, 255]; the higher the more priority over other topics

/twist_mux:
  ros__parameters:
    topics:
      navigation:
        topic   : cmd_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 10
      keyboard:
        topic   : key_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 90
      rviz:
        topic   : rviz_joy_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 100
      joystick:
        topic   : joy_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 100
      webgui_joystick:
        topic   : tab_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 100
      assisted_teleop:
        topic   : assisted_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 200
      docking:
        topic   : docking_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 210

controller_configuration.locks_yaml:
# Locks to stop the twist mux.
# For each lock:
# - topic   : input topic that provides the lock; it must be of type std_msgs::Bool?!!! 
# - timeout : == 0.0 -> not used
#              > 0.0 -> the lock is supposed to published at a certain frequency in order
#                       to detect that the publisher is alive; the timeout in seconds allows
#                       to detect that, and if the publisher dies we will enable the lock
# - priority: priority in the range [0, 255], so all the topics with priority lower than it
#             will be stopped/disabled

/twist_mux:
  ros__parameters:
    locks:
      joystick:
        topic   : joy_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 100
      assisted_teleop:
        topic   : assisted_teleop_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 200
      charging:
        topic   : power/is_charging
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 210

# Input topics handled/muxed by the twist mux.

source_context.timing_scope: Requested window follows upstream task bookkeeping and its sec.nanosec conversion. A recorded navigation success does not establish a safety-speed policy or a measured cause of slowness.

# Locks to stop the twist mux.
# For each lock:
# - topic   : input topic that provides the lock; it must be of type std_msgs::Bool?!!! 
# - timeout : == 0.0 -> not used
#              > 0.0 -> the lock is supposed to published at a certain frequency in order
#                       to detect that the publisher is alive; the timeout in seconds allows
#                       to detect that, and if the publisher dies we will enable the lock
# - priority: priority in the range [0, 255], so all the topics with priority lower than it
#             will be stopped/disabled

/twist_mux:
  ros__parameters:
    locks:
      joystick:
        topic   : joy_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 100
      assisted_teleop:
        topic   : assisted_teleop_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 200

        topic   : power/is_charging
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 210

controller_configuration.locks_yaml:
# Locks to stop the twist mux.
# For each lock:
# - topic   : input topic that provides the lock; it must be of type std_msgs::Bool?!!! 
# - timeout : == 0.0 -> not used
#              > 0.0 -> the lock is supposed to published at a certain frequency in order
#                       to detect that the publisher is alive; the timeout in seconds allows
#                       to detect that, and if the publisher dies we will enable the lock
# - priority: priority in the range [0, 255], so all the topics with priority lower than it
#             will be stopped/disabled

/twist_mux:
  ros__parameters:
    locks:
      joystick:
        topic   : joy_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 100
      assisted_teleop:
        topic   : assisted_teleop_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 200
      charging:
        topic   : power/is_charging
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 210
controller_configuration.topics_yaml:
# Input topics handled/muxed by the twist mux.
# For each topic:
# - name    : name identifier to select the topic
# - topic   : input topic of geometry_msgs::Twist type
# - timeout : timeout in seconds to start discarding old messages, and use 0.0 speed instead
# - priority: priority in the range [0, 255]; the higher the more priority over other topics

/twist_mux:
  ros__parameters:
    topics:
      navigation:
        topic   : cmd_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 10
      keyboard:
        topic   : key_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 90
      rviz:
        topic   : rviz_joy_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 100
      joystick:
        topic   : joy_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 100
      webgui_joystick:
        topic   : tab_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 100
      assisted_teleop:
        topic   : assisted_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 200
      docking:
        topic   : docking_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 210

controller_configuration.locks_yaml:
# Locks to stop the twist mux.
# For each lock:
# - topic   : input topic that provides the lock; it must be of type std_msgs::Bool?!!! 
# - timeout : == 0.0 -> not used
#              > 0.0 -> the lock is supposed to published at a certain frequency in order
#                       to detect that the publisher is alive; the timeout in seconds allows
#                       to detect that, and if the publisher dies we will enable the lock
# - priority: priority in the range [0, 255], so all the topics with priority lower than it
#             will be stopped/disabled

/twist_mux:
  ros__parameters:
    locks:
      joystick:
        topic   : joy_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 100
      assisted_teleop:
        topic   : assisted_teleop_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 200
      charging:
        topic   : power/is_charging
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 210

# Input topics handled/muxed by the twist mux.

/twist_mux:
  ros__parameters:
    topics:
      navigation:
        topic   : cmd_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 10

        topic   : key_vel

        topic   : rviz_joy_vel

        topic   : joy_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 100

        topic   : tab_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 100
      assisted_teleop:
        topic   : assisted_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 200
      docking:
        topic   : docking_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 210

controller_configuration.locks_yaml:
# Locks to stop the twist mux.
# For each lock:
# - topic   : input topic that provides the lock; it must be of type std_msgs::Bool?!!! 
# - timeout : == 0.0 -> not used
#              > 0.0 -> the lock is supposed to published at a certain frequency in order
#                       to detect that the publisher is alive; the timeout in seconds allows
#                       to detect that, and if the publisher dies we will enable the lock
# - priority: priority in the range [0, 255], so all the topics with priority lower than it
#             will be stopped/disabled

/twist_mux:
  ros__parameters:
    locks:
      joystick:
        topic   : joy_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 100
      assisted_teleop:
        topic   : assisted_teleop_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 200
      charging:
        topic   : power/is_charging
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 210
controller_configuration.topics_yaml:
# Input topics handled/muxed by the twist mux.
# For each topic:
# - name    : name identifier to select the topic
# - topic   : input topic of geometry_msgs::Twist type
# - timeout : timeout in seconds to start discarding old messages, and use 0.0 speed instead
# - priority: priority in the range [0, 255]; the higher the more priority over other topics

/twist_mux:
  ros__parameters:
    topics:
      navigation:
        topic   : cmd_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 10
      keyboard:
        topic   : key_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 90
      rviz:
        topic   : rviz_joy_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 100
      joystick:
        topic   : joy_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 100
      webgui_joystick:
        topic   : tab_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 100
      assisted_teleop:
        topic   : assisted_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 200
      docking:
        topic   : docking_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 210

controller_configuration.locks_yaml:
# Locks to stop the twist mux.
# For each lock:
# - topic   : input topic that provides the lock; it must be of type std_msgs::Bool?!!! 
# - timeout : == 0.0 -> not used
#              > 0.0 -> the lock is supposed to published at a certain frequency in order
#                       to detect that the publisher is alive; the timeout in seconds allows
#                       to detect that, and if the publisher dies we will enable the lock
# - priority: priority in the range [0, 255], so all the topics with priority lower than it
#             will be stopped/disabled

/twist_mux:
  ros__parameters:
    locks:
      joystick:
        topic   : joy_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 100
      assisted_teleop:
        topic   : assisted_teleop_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 200
      charging:
        topic   : power/is_charging
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 210
controller_configuration.topics_yaml:
# Input topics handled/muxed by the twist mux.
# For each topic:
# - name    : name identifier to select the topic
# - topic   : input topic of geometry_msgs::Twist type
# - timeout : timeout in seconds to start discarding old messages, and use 0.0 speed instead
# - priority: priority in the range [0, 255]; the higher the more priority over other topics

/twist_mux:
  ros__parameters:
    topics:
      navigation:
        topic   : cmd_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 10
      keyboard:
        topic   : key_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 90
      rviz:
        topic   : rviz_joy_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 100
      joystick:
        topic   : joy_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 100
      webgui_joystick:
        topic   : tab_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 100
      assisted_teleop:
        topic   : assisted_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 200
      docking:
        topic   : docking_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 210

Any supplied runtime snapshots are observed parameter-service and ROS-graph evidence only at their explicit native simulated-clock stamps. Absent or masked snapshots remain unknown. source_context.event_scope: Planner/progress failure and clearing-request logs are software execution evidence, not direct geometry or unique physical causes. No supplied costmap/scan/path measurement proves an obstacle or moving obstacle. A clearing request does not prove completed clearing.
source_context.indicator_semantics: The released component maps /joy_priority to manual selection and /power/is_charging to charging selection. In this adapted simulation these Bool states are supervisor interlock indicators, not proof of a human joystick action or physical battery charging. The genuine public controller configuration is supplied below. Only measurements explicitly visible in the packet can establish applied output or physical motion; missing measurements remain unknown.
source_context.localization_semantics: The original callback appends a high-uncertainty diagnostic after its count exceeds five samples with mean XY covariance or orientation variance above .2. Its count decrements on low samples; this is preserved, not a new localization detector.
source_context.missingness: Unavailable evidence is unknown; do not replace it with false, zero, success or normal behavior.
source_context.motion_window_scope: Odometry is restricted to recorded simulated ROS stamps within instrumented driver observations of acceptance-to-result/disposition. The recorded sample extent, boundary gaps and maximum internal gap remain explicit. Driver observations are software protocol evidence, not physical arrival. Command summaries retain their recording scope; no receipt-clock conversion or TF transform is inferred.
source_context.navigation_task_scope: This adapted no-arm simulation executes navigation only. Recorded task labels are reported software metadata, not evidence of manipulation, item delivery or an independently verified room/zone. A label such as kitchen is not a measured semantic location. Do not invent unexecuted skills.
source_context.outcome_measurement_scope: Navigation/task status is a reported software outcome. Reported success alone does not establish measured motion or physical goal attainment. A software status and instrumented motion observation may differ; describe both when visible without inventing a reason for the difference. Unavailable motion or goal/pose/frame/time evidence remains unknown.
source_context.timing_scope: Requested window follows upstream task bookkeeping and its sec.nanosec conversion. A recorded navigation success does not establish a safety-speed policy or a measured cause of slowness.

controller_configuration.locks_yaml:
# Locks to stop the twist mux.
# For each lock:
# - topic   : input topic that provides the lock; it must be of type std_msgs::Bool?!!! 
# - timeout : == 0.0 -> not used
#              > 0.0 -> the lock is supposed to published at a certain frequency in order
#                       to detect that the publisher is alive; the timeout in seconds allows
#                       to detect that, and if the publisher dies we will enable the lock
# - priority: priority in the range [0, 255], so all the topics with priority lower than it
#             will be stopped/disabled

/twist_mux:
  ros__parameters:
    locks:
      joystick:
        topic   : joy_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 100
      assisted_teleop:
        topic   : assisted_teleop_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 200
      charging:
        topic   : power/is_charging
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 210

# Locks to stop the twist mux.

# Locks to stop the twist mux.
# For each lock:
# - topic   : input topic that provides the lock; it must be of type std_msgs::Bool?!!! 
# - timeout : == 0.0 -> not used
#              > 0.0 -> the lock is supposed to published at a certain frequency in order
#                       to detect that the publisher is alive; the timeout in seconds allows
#                       to detect that, and if the publisher dies we will enable the lock
# - priority: priority in the range [0, 255], so all the topics with priority lower than it
#             will be stopped/disabled

/twist_mux:
  ros__parameters:
    locks:
      joystick:
        topic   : joy_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 100
      assisted_teleop:
        topic   : assisted_teleop_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 200

        topic   : power/is_charging
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 210

controller_configuration.locks_yaml:
# Locks to stop the twist mux.
# For each lock:
# - topic   : input topic that provides the lock; it must be of type std_msgs::Bool?!!! 
# - timeout : == 0.0 -> not used
#              > 0.0 -> the lock is supposed to published at a certain frequency in order
#                       to detect that the publisher is alive; the timeout in seconds allows
#                       to detect that, and if the publisher dies we will enable the lock
# - priority: priority in the range [0, 255], so all the topics with priority lower than it
#             will be stopped/disabled

/twist_mux:
  ros__parameters:
    locks:
      joystick:
        topic   : joy_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 100
      assisted_teleop:
        topic   : assisted_teleop_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 200
      charging:
        topic   : power/is_charging
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 210
controller_configuration.topics_yaml:
# Input topics handled/muxed by the twist mux.
# For each topic:
# - name    : name identifier to select the topic
# - topic   : input topic of geometry_msgs::Twist type
# - timeout : timeout in seconds to start discarding old messages, and use 0.0 speed instead
# - priority: priority in the range [0, 255]; the higher the more priority over other topics

/twist_mux:
  ros__parameters:
    topics:
      navigation:
        topic   : cmd_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 10
      keyboard:
        topic   : key_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 90
      rviz:
        topic   : rviz_joy_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 100
      joystick:
        topic   : joy_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 100
      webgui_joystick:
        topic   : tab_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 100
      assisted_teleop:
        topic   : assisted_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 200
      docking:
        topic   : docking_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 210

source_context.controller_source_scope: Static public configuration licenses source-qualified priority rules. Any supplied runtime snapshots are observed parameter-service and ROS-graph evidence only at their explicit native simulated-clock stamps. Absent or masked snapshots remain unknown. Two matching boundary snapshots do not prove continuous wiring or absence of intervening changes. Neither configuration nor graph alone proves message delivery, applied torque, physical arrival, or a unique physical cause.
source_context.event_scope: Planner/progress failure and clearing-request logs are software execution evidence, not direct geometry or unique physical causes. No supplied costmap/scan/path measurement proves an obstacle or moving obstacle. A clearing request does not prove completed clearing.
source_context.indicator_semantics: The released component maps /joy_priority to manual selection and /power/is_charging to charging selection. In this adapted simulation these Bool states are supervisor interlock indicators, not proof of a human joystick action or physical battery charging. The genuine public controller configuration is supplied below. Only measurements explicitly visible in the packet can establish applied output or physical motion; missing measurements remain unknown.
source_context.localization_semantics: The original callback appends a high-uncertainty diagnostic after its count exceeds five samples with mean XY covariance or orientation variance above .2. Its count decrements on low samples; this is preserved, not a new localization detector.
source_context.missingness: Unavailable evidence is unknown; do not replace it with false, zero, success or normal behavior.
source_context.motion_window_scope: Odometry is restricted to recorded simulated ROS stamps within instrumented driver observations of acceptance-to-result/disposition. The recorded sample extent, boundary gaps and maximum internal gap remain explicit. Driver observations are software protocol evidence, not physical arrival. Command summaries retain their recording scope; no receipt-clock conversion or TF transform is inferred.
source_context.navigation_task_scope: This adapted no-arm simulation executes navigation only. Recorded task labels are reported software metadata, not evidence of manipulation, item delivery or an independently verified room/zone. A label such as kitchen is not a measured semantic location. Do not invent unexecuted skills.
source_context.outcome_measurement_scope: Navigation/task status is a reported software outcome. Reported success alone does not establish measured motion or physical goal attainment. A software status and instrumented motion observation may differ; describe both when visible without inventing a reason for the difference. Unavailable motion or goal/pose/frame/time evidence remains unknown.
source_context.timing_scope: Requested window follows upstream task bookkeeping and its sec.nanosec conversion. A recorded navigation success does not establish a safety-speed policy or a measured cause of slowness.

controller_configuration.locks_yaml:
# Locks to stop the twist mux.
# For each lock:
# - topic   : input topic that provides the lock; it must be of type std_msgs::Bool?!!! 
# - timeout : == 0.0 -> not used
#              > 0.0 -> the lock is supposed to published at a certain frequency in order
#                       to detect that the publisher is alive; the timeout in seconds allows
#                       to detect that, and if the publisher dies we will enable the lock
# - priority: priority in the range [0, 255], so all the topics with priority lower than it
#             will be stopped/disabled

/twist_mux:
  ros__parameters:
    locks:
      joystick:
        topic   : joy_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 100
      assisted_teleop:
        topic   : assisted_teleop_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 200
      charging:
        topic   : power/is_charging
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 210

# Input topics handled/muxed by the twist mux.
# For each topic:
# - name    : name identifier to select the topic
# - topic   : input topic of geometry_msgs::Twist type
# - timeout : timeout in seconds to start discarding old messages, and use 0.0 speed instead
# - priority: priority in the range [0, 255]; the higher the more priority over other topics

/twist_mux:
  ros__parameters:
    topics:
      navigation:
        topic   : cmd_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 10
      keyboard:
        topic   : key_vel
        timeout : 0.5

        topic   : rviz_joy_vel

        priority: 100

        topic   : joy_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 100
      webgui_joystick:
        topic   : tab_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 100
      assisted_teleop:
        topic   : assisted_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 200
      docking:
        topic   : docking_vel
        timeout : 0.5

# Locks to stop the twist mux.
# For each lock:
# - topic   : input topic that provides the lock; it must be of type std_msgs::Bool?!!! 
# - timeout : == 0.0 -> not used
#              > 0.0 -> the lock is supposed to published at a certain frequency in order
#                       to detect that the publisher is alive; the timeout in seconds allows
#                       to detect that, and if the publisher dies we will enable the lock
# - priority: priority in the range [0, 255], so all the topics with priority lower than it
#             will be stopped/disabled

/twist_mux:
  ros__parameters:
    locks:
      joystick:
        topic   : joy_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 100
      assisted_teleop:
        topic   : assisted_teleop_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 200

        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 210

controller_configuration.locks_yaml:
# Locks to stop the twist mux.
# For each lock:
# - topic   : input topic that provides the lock; it must be of type std_msgs::Bool?!!! 
# - timeout : == 0.0 -> not used
#              > 0.0 -> the lock is supposed to published at a certain frequency in order
#                       to detect that the publisher is alive; the timeout in seconds allows
#                       to detect that, and if the publisher dies we will enable the lock
# - priority: priority in the range [0, 255], so all the topics with priority lower than it
#             will be stopped/disabled

/twist_mux:
  ros__parameters:
    locks:
      joystick:
        topic   : joy_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 100
      assisted_teleop:
        topic   : assisted_teleop_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 200
      charging:
        topic   : power/is_charging
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 210
controller_configuration.topics_yaml:
# Input topics handled/muxed by the twist mux.
# For each topic:
# - name    : name identifier to select the topic
# - topic   : input topic of geometry_msgs::Twist type
# - timeout : timeout in seconds to start discarding old messages, and use 0.0 speed instead
# - priority: priority in the range [0, 255]; the higher the more priority over other topics

/twist_mux:
  ros__parameters:
    topics:
      navigation:
        topic   : cmd_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 10
      keyboard:
        topic   : key_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 90
      rviz:
        topic   : rviz_joy_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 100
      joystick:
        topic   : joy_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 100
      webgui_joystick:
        topic   : tab_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 100
      assisted_teleop:
        topic   : assisted_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 200
      docking:
        topic   : docking_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 210

source_context.controller_source_scope: Static public configuration licenses source-qualified priority rules. Any supplied runtime snapshots are observed parameter-service and ROS-graph evidence only at their explicit native simulated-clock stamps. Absent or masked snapshots remain unknown. Two matching boundary snapshots do not prove continuous wiring or absence of intervening changes. Neither configuration nor graph alone proves message delivery, applied torque, physical arrival, or a unique physical cause.
source_context.event_scope: Planner/progress failure and clearing-request logs are software execution evidence, not direct geometry or unique physical causes. No supplied costmap/scan/path measurement proves an obstacle or moving obstacle. A clearing request does not prove completed clearing.
source_context.indicator_semantics: The released component maps /joy_priority to manual selection and /power/is_charging to charging selection. In this adapted simulation these Bool states are supervisor interlock indicators, not proof of a human joystick action or physical battery charging. The genuine public controller configuration is supplied below. Only measurements explicitly visible in the packet can establish applied output or physical motion; missing measurements remain unknown.
source_context.localization_semantics: The original callback appends a high-uncertainty diagnostic after its count exceeds five samples with mean XY covariance or orientation variance above .2. Its count decrements on low samples; this is preserved, not a new localization detector.
source_context.missingness: Unavailable evidence is unknown; do not replace it with false, zero, success or normal behavior.
source_context.motion_window_scope: Odometry is restricted to recorded simulated ROS stamps within instrumented driver observations of acceptance-to-result/disposition. The recorded sample extent, boundary gaps and maximum internal gap remain explicit. Driver observations are software protocol evidence, not physical arrival. Command summaries retain their recording scope; no receipt-clock conversion or TF transform is inferred.
source_context.navigation_task_scope: This adapted no-arm simulation executes navigation only. Recorded task labels are reported software metadata, not evidence of manipulation, item delivery or an independently verified room/zone. A label such as kitchen is not a measured semantic location. Do not invent unexecuted skills.
source_context.outcome_measurement_scope: Navigation/task status is a reported software outcome. Reported success alone does not establish measured motion or physical goal attainment. A software status and instrumented motion observation may differ; describe both when visible without inventing a reason for the difference. Unavailable motion or goal/pose/frame/time evidence remains unknown.
source_context.timing_scope: Requested window follows upstream task bookkeeping and its sec.nanosec conversion. A recorded navigation success does not establish a safety-speed policy or a measured cause of slowness.

controller_configuration.locks_yaml:
# Locks to stop the twist mux.
# For each lock:
# - topic   : input topic that provides the lock; it must be of type std_msgs::Bool?!!! 
# - timeout : == 0.0 -> not used
#              > 0.0 -> the lock is supposed to published at a certain frequency in order
#                       to detect that the publisher is alive; the timeout in seconds allows
#                       to detect that, and if the publisher dies we will enable the lock
# - priority: priority in the range [0, 255], so all the topics with priority lower than it
#             will be stopped/disabled

/twist_mux:
  ros__parameters:
    locks:
      joystick:
        topic   : joy_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 100
      assisted_teleop:
        topic   : assisted_teleop_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 200
      charging:
        topic   : power/is_charging
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 210

controller_configuration.locks_yaml:
# Locks to stop the twist mux.
# For each lock:
# - topic   : input topic that provides the lock; it must be of type std_msgs::Bool?!!! 
# - timeout : == 0.0 -> not used
#              > 0.0 -> the lock is supposed to published at a certain frequency in order
#                       to detect that the publisher is alive; the timeout in seconds allows
#                       to detect that, and if the publisher dies we will enable the lock
# - priority: priority in the range [0, 255], so all the topics with priority lower than it
#             will be stopped/disabled

/twist_mux:
  ros__parameters:
    locks:
      joystick:
        topic   : joy_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 100
      assisted_teleop:
        topic   : assisted_teleop_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 200
      charging:
        topic   : power/is_charging
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 210
controller_configuration.topics_yaml:
# Input topics handled/muxed by the twist mux.
# For each topic:
# - name    : name identifier to select the topic
# - topic   : input topic of geometry_msgs::Twist type
# - timeout : timeout in seconds to start discarding old messages, and use 0.0 speed instead
# - priority: priority in the range [0, 255]; the higher the more priority over other topics

/twist_mux:
  ros__parameters:
    topics:
      navigation:
        topic   : cmd_vel
        timeout : 0.5

        priority: 100

        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 100
      assisted_teleop:
        topic   : assisted_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 200

controller_configuration.locks_yaml:
# Locks to stop the twist mux.
# For each lock:
# - topic   : input topic that provides the lock; it must be of type std_msgs::Bool?!!! 
# - timeout : == 0.0 -> not used
#              > 0.0 -> the lock is supposed to published at a certain frequency in order
#                       to detect that the publisher is alive; the timeout in seconds allows
#                       to detect that, and if the publisher dies we will enable the lock
# - priority: priority in the range [0, 255], so all the topics with priority lower than it
#             will be stopped/disabled

/twist_mux:
  ros__parameters:
    locks:
      joystick:
        topic   : joy_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 100
      assisted_teleop:
        topic   : assisted_teleop_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 200

        priority: 210

controller_configuration.locks_yaml:
# Locks to stop the twist mux.
# For each lock:
# - topic   : input topic that provides the lock; it must be of type std_msgs::Bool?!!! 
# - timeout : == 0.0 -> not used
#              > 0.0 -> the lock is supposed to published at a certain frequency in order
#                       to detect that the publisher is alive; the timeout in seconds allows
#                       to detect that, and if the publisher dies we will enable the lock
# - priority: priority in the range [0, 255], so all the topics with priority lower than it
#             will be stopped/disabled

/twist_mux:
  ros__parameters:
    locks:
      joystick:
        topic   : joy_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 100
      assisted_teleop:
        topic   : assisted_teleop_priority
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 200
      charging:
        topic   : power/is_charging
        timeout : 0.0
        priority: 210
controller_configuration.topics_yaml:
# Input topics handled/muxed by the twist mux.
# For each topic:
# - name    : name identifier to select the topic
# - topic   : input topic of geometry_msgs::Twist type
# - timeout : timeout in seconds to start discarding old messages, and use 0.0 speed instead
# - priority: priority in the range [0, 255]; the higher the more priority over other topics

/twist_mux:
  ros__parameters:
    topics:
      navigation:
        topic   : cmd_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 10
      keyboard:
        topic   : key_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 90
      rviz:
        topic   : rviz_joy_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 100
      joystick:
        topic   : joy_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 100
      webgui_joystick:
        topic   : tab_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 100
      assisted_teleop:
        topic   : assisted_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 200
      docking:
        topic   : docking_vel
        timeout : 0.5
        priority: 210
